key_insight: Exponential moving averages used by Adam-like optimizers can be viewed as online linear-regressor training via gradient flow, enabling a low-rank factorization of optimizer states that preserves optimizer behavior while drastically cutting memory.
problem_solved: Reduces the large memory overhead caused by storing full first- and second-order momentum matrices during pre-training of large models, which limits scalability and increases training cost.
method: Reinterpret EMA momenta as solutions of an online linear regression problem (gradient flow view) to reveal their low-dimensional structure.
Approximate optimizer states with a low-rank factorization (LoRA-Pre) and update factors in the low-dimensional subspace instead of full matrices.
Maintain optimizer performance with reduced state size via efficient low-rank updates and theoretical/empirical validation on pre-training workloads.
impact: Enables large-model pre-training with substantially lower GPU memory and similar convergence/quality, letting practitioners scale models or batch sizes and reduce infrastructure cost without changing training recipes.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: EMA → online linear regression (gradient-flow equivalence) showing the conceptual reframe.
Schematic: full-matrix momenta vs low-rank factorized momenta side-by-side (memory footprint callouts).
Bar chart: GPU memory / throughput / training time comparisons between Adam/Muon and LoRA-Pre across model sizes.
Curve plot: validation loss or downstream metric vs steps showing comparable convergence of LoRA-Pre and baseline optimizers.
paper_title: Taming Momentum: Rethinking Optimizer States Through Low-Rank Approximation
paper_authors: Zhengbo Wang, Jian Liang, Ran He, Zilei Wang, Tieniu Tan
